'''Kazukuru''' is an extinct language that was once spoken in [[New Georgia]], [[Solomon Islands]]. The Dororo and Guliguli languages (if they even existed) were transcriptional variants, dialects, or closely related. The speakers of Kazukuru gradually merged with the [[Roviana language|Roviana]] people from the sixteenth century onward and adopted Roviana as their language.  Kazukuru was last recorded in the early twentieth century when its speakers were in the last stages of language shift. Today, Kazukuru is the name of a clan in the Roviana people group.

==History of documentation==
Most of what is known about Kazukuru was collected by W.H.L. Waterhouse and published with S.H. Ray in an article in 1931. Some additional Kazukuru data and the only information on Dororo and Guliguli (two short wordlists) were published by Peter Lanyon-Orgill in 1953.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lanyon-Orgill |first=Peter A. |date=1953 |title=The Papuan languages of the New Georgian Archipelago, Solomon Islands |journal=Journal of Austronesian Studies |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=122–138}}</ref> Davis (2003) is skeptical that Guliguli ever existed, since the word {{Lang|hoa|guliguli}} has an obscene meaning in the neighboring [[Hoava language]], and there is no memory among Hoava speakers of a neighboring language with that name.<ref>{{Cite book |title=A Grammar of the Hoava language, Western Solomons |last=Davis |first=Karen |date=2003 |publisher=Pacific Linguistics |isbn=978-0-85883-502-3 |series=Pacific Linguistics 535 |location=Canberra |doi=10.15144/PL-535 |hdl=1885/146158 |doi-access=free |hdl-access=free}}</ref> Guliguli was probably either a dialect of Kazukuru, a naive transcription of the name ''Kazukuru'', or even a hoax.<ref name="Dunn&Ross">{{Cite journal |last1=Dunn |first1=Michael |last2=Ross |first2=Malcolm |date=2007 |title=Is Kazukuru Really Non-Austronesian? |url=http://pubman.mpdl.mpg.de/pubman/item/escidoc:60507/component/escidoc:60508/dunn_2007_is+kazukuru.pdf |journal=Oceanic Linguistics |volume=46 |issue=1 |pages=210–231 |doi=10.1353/ol.2007.0018 |jstor=4499986|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0013-1EBB-9 |s2cid=146355432 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

==Classification==
[[Arthur Capell]] suggested that Kazukuru was a non-Austronesian ([[Papuan languages|Papuan]]) language, and [[Stephen Wurm]] accordingly placed all three languages in a 'Kazukuru family' within the [[East Papuan languages|East Papuan]] phylum. However, Michael Dunn and [[Malcolm Ross (linguist)|Malcolm Ross]] (2007) argue that the structure, phonology and lexicon of Kazukuru are strikingly similar to [[Oceanic languages]] and that Kazukuru almost certainly was an Oceanic language, related to other New Georgia languages such as [[Roviana language|Roviana]], [[Hoava language|Hoava]] and [[Ghanongga language|Ghanongga]]. The alleged Dororo and Guliguli wordlists are so similar to the recorded Kazukuru wordlist that they are almost certainly different transcriptions of the same language.<ref name=Dunn&Ross/>
